To draw the projections of the square pyramid:

1. **Initial Position (Axis perpendicular to HP):**
   * Assume the pyramid rests with its base on the HP such that one of its base corners is oriented suitably (e.g., edge making equal inclination or corner pointing forward). Since a *corner* is on HP, orient the square base so that a diagonal is perpendicular to VP or parallel, making it easier to tilt.
   * Draw the top view as a square of side $30\text{ mm}$ with its diagonals intersecting at the axis center $o$.
   * Project the front view as a triangle with base equal to the side/diagonal projected and height $60\text{ mm}$.
2. **Final Position (Axis inclined at $30^	ext{o}$ to HP):**
   * Tilt the front view of the axis (and thus the whole front view) by $30^	ext{o}$ to the $XY$ line such that the designated corner touches the $XY$ line (representing HP).
   * Project the final top view downwards from the tilted front view and horizontally from the initial top view to locate the final coordinates of the base corners and the apex $O$.
proTip: When a solid rests on a corner on the HP, tilt the base first assuming an edge condition, then shift the axis inclination while keeping the corner fixed on the reference line.
